artifacts.summary: Maps public litter bins and measures how well the area is served with places to throw away waste while out on foot. Good bin provision supports clean, pleasant and walkable streets.

artifacts.name: Statistics
artifacts.summary: Spread, inequality and clustering measures for the area’s public bins. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.27. 0 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of public bins density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 10 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over public bins density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do public bins track where people live? Public bins per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its public bins per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita
artifacts.summary: Public bins per 1,000 residents across the sub-areas — provision relative to need. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of public bins per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Coverage on foot
artifacts.summary: About 88% of the area is within 300 m on foot of a public bin. About 99% of residents are within reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The area of interest split into the part within reach (on foot) of any feature and the part beyond it. Reachability is computed using straight-line distance.

The area of interest split into the part within reach (by wheelchair) of any feature and the part beyond it. Reachability is computed using straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Public bins heatmap
artifacts.summary: A gridded density of public bins across the area — brighter means more. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area of interest, each cell shaded by how many public bins fall within it. It reveals clusters and gaps that individual points can hide.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Public bins density surface
artifacts.summary: A smoothed, continuous density surface of public bins (kernel-style). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of public bins: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest public bin
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest public bin from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest public bin. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness
artifacts.summary: How recently each public bin was last edited in OpenStreetMap (median 2 yr ago). Darker = longer since the last edit. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: bins · reachability: straight-line distance.
